title: How a repeater works
blurb: It listens on one frequency and retransmits on another.

lines.caption: Two handheld radios often cannot reach each other. A hill or a building is in the way.
A repeater is a station up high, on a tower or a hilltop, where it can hear them both.
It listens on one frequency and, at the same moment, retransmits what it hears on another.
The difference between its transmit and receive frequencies is called the repeater offset.
On the 2 meter band, a common offset is plus or minus 600 kHz.
On the 70 centimeter band, a common offset is plus or minus 5 MHz.
Many repeaters also want a tone. CTCSS is a sub-audible tone, sent along with your voice, that opens the repeater's squelch.
If you can hear a repeater but cannot get into it, check your offset and your tone.
